idea.why: One specialist per data source and a third agent whose system message explicitly forbids re-sorting, so the three roles do not overlap. Fan-out then rejoin matches the real dependency shape. One point off because a full day of mail is stuffed whole into a single prompt with no cap.

structure.why: Purpose-built nodes throughout and not a single Code node. Seventeen nodes is proportionate given each agent legitimately costs a model plus a parser. Three separate model nodes is defensible because the tiers differ, but the template carries dense inline map and join logic.

connections.why: The trigger fans out rather than chaining two unrelated fetches, each branch stays linear where genuinely dependent, and the streams rejoin at a real Merge before synthesis. Minor awkwardness: the merged payload is not consumed, so the Merge functions mostly as a barrier.

answer.why: Every clause of the brief lands, with per-section empty states and continueRegularOutput so one failure does not kill the briefing. It is an emailed page rather than one you can open on demand, and the recipient is a placeholder needing a fill.

appraisal: Finds the shape the brief implies rather than the first that compiles: two source-specific agents in parallel, a synthesis agent told not to repeat their work, and a rendering step that is a template rather than string-building. The wiring is honest about dependencies. The weak spots are narrow: an uncapped fetch means a busy inbox pours hundreds of messages into one prompt, the Merge is a barrier whose payload nobody reads, and the dashboard exists only as an email. A knowledgeable user would bound the fetch first, then add a webhook path serving the same HTML so the briefing survives being deleted from the inbox.
